items.quote: the Generation, Dignity, & Excelency OF THE MICROCOSM, Or Little World MAN
items.what: THE MICROCOSM, Or Little World MAN
items.note: The heading announces the section's subject and names man the Microcosm or Little World; it promises three heads: Generation, Dignity, Excelency.

items.quote: For a man to know God & lightly esteem of his own selfe is the highest and profitable knowledge
items.note: The margin note sets knowing God and esteeming oneself lightly as the highest knowledge.

items.quote: the most excellent Phylosophy is that which enlightens the mind to the right knowledge of it selfe
items.note: The best philosophy is defined by its object: the mind's right knowledge of itself.

items.quote: to be ignorant of that knowledge is the greatest shame and most pestilent disease of the mind
items.note: Ignorance of self-knowledge is called a disease of the mind.

items.name: Trismegistus
items.quote: Ignorance, saith Trismegistus to his Son Tat, is the greatest Enemy and principall Tormenter in every Man
items.note: Words given to Trismegistus, addressed to his son Tat, used in support of the point on ignorance.

items.name: Luke 16
items.quote: Luke 16
items.note: Margin reference beside 'Woe be to thee ô Man' and the neglected patrimony and Talent.

items.quote: who considerest not the Treasure that is hid in thy earthen vessell, and may thereout be digged
items.note: A treasure is said to be hidden in man's 'earthen vessell' and able to be dug out; the figure of hidden treasure in man.

items.name: 2 Cor. 4.
items.quote: 2 Cor. 4.
items.note: Margin reference beside the treasure in the earthen vessel.

items.quote: he be more in us then we are in our selves, inasmuch as the Spirit of God dwelleth in the midst of our hearts
items.note: God is said to be within man, more than man is in himself, because the Spirit dwells in the heart.

items.name: John 14.17.20.
items.note: Margin reference beside 'Thou seest not God in thy selfe, whom the world seeth not, neither can receive'.

items.quote: that Divine lesson that God hath set us, KNOW THY SELFE
items.note: Set in capitals and named a Divine lesson. The sentence before it reads 'we can learn more in the whole course of our life then' this lesson, as given; a margin note in foreign script (N081, a gap) stands beside it.

items.name: Agryppa
items.quote: it is for a man to know Himselfe; according to the Oracle of Apollo written over the doors of his Temple at Delphos
items.note: Agryppa is reported as saying that true Wisdome and Eternall Happinesse lie in knowing oneself, matched to the Oracle of Apollo at Delphos.

items.name: August.
items.quote: The first knowledge of God is to know what man is. August.
items.note: Margin note ascribed to August., beside Agryppa's words: knowledge of God begins with knowing man.

items.quote: man hath the true and Reall possession of all things and Natures in himselfe, as also the speciall and perfect Image even of the Creator of all things
items.note: Man holds all things and natures in himself and the image of the Creator.

items.quote: the knowledge of all things and natures, and of the Creator himselfe (wherein alone true Wisdome and Blessednesse consisteth) must take its rise from the knowledge of a mans selfe
items.note: Knowledge of all things and of God starts from self-knowledge; stated as a consequence of the previous point.

items.quote: as in a kind of Deified glasse, behold and understand all things
items.note: Man knowing himself is likened to a 'Deified glasse' in which all things are seen; a figure of man as mirror.

items.name: David
items.quote: David saith, Psal. 139.14. I am fearfully and wonderfully made, marvellous are thy works.
items.note: David's words cited in support of man's wonderful make.

items.quote: He that knoweth himselfe knows God; for God will dwell no where but in man, in whom he is most plaine to be seen. We see God from within.
items.note: The margin note equates knowing oneself with knowing God and says God is seen from within.

items.quote: He that knoweth not himselfe cannot have any true intrinsecall and essentiall knowledge of things, but like a bruit beast, what he knows without him, shall remaine without him
items.note: Without self-knowledge, knowledge of things stays outside the man, as with a beast.

items.quote: but that onely which is inwardly received by Essentiall knowledge in the secret understanding
items.note: Only knowledge received inwardly, called Essentiall knowledge in the 'secret understanding', abides; all other knowledge is forgotten.

items.quote: which Essential intrinsecall knowledge is not from flesh and blood, nor from the multitude of Books and reading, nor from the abundants of Experience and old age
items.note: The text says what this knowledge does not come from: not flesh and blood, books, reading, experience or age.

items.name: Dionys.
items.quote: Dionys. lib. Divinors Nominum.
items.note: Margin note naming Dionys. and a book beside the list of what essential knowledge does not come from.

items.quote: the mind of man is perfected and compleated by a passive reception of Divine things; not by study and paines; but by patience and submission
items.note: How the mind is perfected: by passive reception, patience and submission, not by study.

items.quote: The whole businesse stands in knowledge, because we are of every thing, and doe carry about every thing in us, even as God himselfe our Father
items.note: Man is said to carry everything within him, as God does.

items.name: Joh. 4. & 17.
items.note: Margin reference beside 'The Son doth equally posesse all things with his Father'.

items.quote: as by sin that Divine Character was darkned in us, so sin being satisfied for, & done away, that Character shines out againe more and more
items.note: A Divine Character in man is darkened by sin and shines again when sin is done away.

items.quote: The Notion of all things is created together with us and in us; and in the very middle of the Spirit by all things hid
items.note: The notion of all things is said to be created in us and hidden in the middle of the Spirit.

items.quote: we are onely to awake out of our slumbring and snorting, who through sin have fallen asleep in the gifts that God hath bestowed upon us
items.note: What is needed is to wake: sin has put man asleep to gifts already in him.

items.name: Plato
items.quote: according to Plato, it is full of all Sciences before it be joyned to the body
items.note: Plato is cited for the understanding being full of all sciences before joining the body. How far the following words on fire in ashes are Plato's is not shown.

items.quote: which being oppressed by the body lyeth hid, as fire rak'd up in ashes, but being rouz'd and stirred up from the said humours it shineth forth and discovereth those riches which before lay hid in their Treasures
items.note: The understanding's knowledge lies hidden like fire raked in ashes and shows its riches when stirred up.

items.quote: stirred up from the said humours
items.note: 'the said humours' points back to humours named before; the lines given do not show where.

items.quote: Unlesse all the Treasures of Heavenly and Earthly wisdome were in us before, surely Christ would never have commanded us to seek
items.note: Christ's command to seek is taken as proof that all wisdom is already in man.

items.quote: When we therefore know our selves aright according to both kinds of Light.
items.note: Self-knowledge is to be had by two kinds of Light; the text then numbers one, '(1) according to the Spirit and Nature'.

items.quote: (1) according to the Spirit and Nature
items.what: (1) according to the Spirit and Nature
items.note: A numbered head; the lines given show only this '(1)', after the margin note mark.

items.quote: we enter into the gate that is opened in us, and we open to God who stands and knocks at the door of our heart
items.note: Right self-knowledge opens a gate in man and the door of the heart to God.

items.quote: From this diligent contemplation & knowledge of a mans self, the true knowledge also of God doth immediately arise (for neither can be absolute & compleat without the other)
items.note: Knowledge of self and of God arise together; neither is complete without the other.

items.quote: the knowledge of him who IS
items.note: God named as 'him who IS', with IS in capitals.

items.quote: God is known when the Light of Nature
items.note: The margin note ties knowing God to understanding the Light of Nature (the next letter is a gap).

items.name: Apoc. 3.20.
items.quote: Apoc. 3.20.
items.note: Margin reference beside God who stands and knocks at the door.

items.name: Dionysius
items.quote: Dionysius saith, that we cannot know God from his own Nature, but from that most orderly disposing of all the Creatures proceeding from himselfe
items.note: Dionysius: God is known not from his nature but from the ordering of the creatures.

items.quote: hold forth as it were images and similitudes of his Divine Presidents or Examples
items.note: Creatures show images of God's 'Presidents or Examples'; the text glosses Presidents as Examples.

items.quote: Man that doth not know God, is not known of God; and he that forsakes and rejecteth the knowledge of God, is rejected of God.
items.note: Whose words these are is UNCLEAR: they follow Dionysius' saying without a mark of where it ends.

items.quote: To be ignorant of God is the Rise or Spring of all diseases, the root of wickedness, by which all vices are increased and grow ripe.
items.note: Ignorance of God is the source of all diseases and vices.

items.quote: The more we know God the more we love him, and stedfastly belive in him. He that believes God by loving of him doth cleave to God, he that doth cleave to God is one Spirit with him.
items.note: The margin note gives a chain: knowing, loving, believing, cleaving, being one Spirit with God.

items.quote: the perfect righteousnesse, true wisdome, and chiefe happinesse of Man is to know his Principle, God the Creator of all things
items.note: God is called man's Principle; knowing and loving him is man's chief happiness.

items.name: our Saviour
items.quote: This is life eternall to know the Father the true God
items.note: Words of 'our Saviour' (John 17.3.) cited for knowledge as eternal life.

items.quote: viz. That the Believer should acknowledge and worship the Trinity, which knowledge onely giveth eternall life
items.note: The text glosses the cited words: the knowledge meant is acknowledging and worshipping the Trinity.

items.quote: he that knoweth God in Christ is made the habitation and Temple of God, and so is Deified
items.note: Knowing God in Christ makes a man God's temple and 'Deified'.

items.quote: as by the knowledge of the visible world we come to the knowledge of the invisible Workman
items.note: From the visible world to the invisible maker, paralleled with Christ leading to the Father.

items.quote: none can rightly know the frame of the world but he that is taught of God
items.note: Right knowledge of the world's frame needs teaching by God.

items.quote: what the Heathen wrote concerning Nature is for the most part false, because their Phylosophy and other abilities were polluted and corrupt
items.note: Heathen writings on Nature are mostly false.

items.quote: many of them were seduced by ignorance rather then malice, the Light of Truth not yet risen to them, nor the Light of Nature as yet kindled by the holy Spirit
items.note: The heathen erred from ignorance; the Light of Nature is said to be kindled by the holy Spirit.

items.quote: All true Phylosophy should be grounded on the Scriptures and so return into God
items.note: True philosophy is to rest on Scripture.

items.quote: that seed which among the Gentiles was choaked for want of the Sun, like that among the thorns
items.note: Knowledge among the Gentiles is figured as seed choked for want of the Sun.

items.quote: No Art can be perfected without Regeneration
items.note: Regeneration is a condition for perfecting any Art.

items.quote: True Phylosophy must be grounded on Christ the corner stone.
items.note: True philosophy rests on Christ.

items.quote: Christians onely in whom the Truth is planted, who have their seed from God, by the means of Regeneration which the Heathen have not
items.note: Only regenerate Christians can use or teach philosophy without error; the heathen are said to lack Regeneration.

items.quote: Divinity is the Fountaine of Naturall and Supernaturall knowledge.
items.note: Margin note: Divinity is the source of both natural and supernatural knowledge.

items.quote: Christians should not be ruled by Heathen Phylosophy.
items.note: Margin note restating the warning against heathen philosophy.

items.quote: the knowledge of God is the Treasury of the whole world wherein all things are laid up
items.note: Knowledge of God is called the treasury in which all things are laid up.

items.quote: For Faith, Hope and Love, follow knowledge, Adhaesion or cleaving to followeth Love, Union follows Adhaesion, in Union is Blessednesse and Wisdome.
items.what: knowledge, Faith, Hope and Love, Adhaesion, Union
items.note: An ordered series of steps ending in Union, where Blessednesse and Wisdome lie.

items.quote: Adhaesion or cleaving to followeth Love
items.note: Adhaesion is glossed as 'cleaving to'.

items.quote: This Regeneration that holy man Hermes and others of clean hearts and godly lives before the Word was incarnate being enlightned by the holy Spirit, though they concealed it among other Secrets
items.note: Hermes and others before the Incarnation knew Regeneration and concealed it among other Secrets.

items.name: Hermes
items.quote: that holy man Hermes
items.note: Hermes is named and called holy, as one who knew Regeneration.

items.quote: they knew it better then many of us who call our selves Christians, and had rather seem to know God then love him
items.note: These earlier men are said to have known Regeneration better than many Christians.

items.quote: This Regeneration that holy man Hermes
items.note: MICRO.8 says Regeneration is what 'the Heathen have not'; here Hermes, before the Word was incarnate, knew Regeneration. The lines given do not say whether Hermes counts among the Heathen.

items.quote: Man whose mind by Christ is united to God, possesseth the true wisdome of all things, and the most absolute knowledge of all Secrets.
items.note: The man united to God through Christ holds knowledge of all Secrets; announced as 'O great miracle!'.

items.name: 1 John 4.
items.quote: 1 John 4.
items.note: Margin references (1 John 4., a book with a gap, John 17) beside the man united to God.

items.quote: he that knoweth himselfe, doth know all things Fundamentally in himselfe, and being set between Time and Eternity, above him he sees God eternall, his Creator
items.note: The self-knower knows all things in himself and is placed between Time and Eternity.

items.quote: after whose image and likenesse he was with other Angells created by an unsearchable love
items.note: Man is said to have been created 'with other Angells'.

items.quote: the immortall Angells his fellows and companions, from whom he differeth onely in body and the Judgement to come
items.note: Man differs from the angels only in body and the Judgement to come.

items.quote: Under him he sees the visible World whereof he is a pattern, and all the Creatures with whom he hath a likenesse, even his parent of whom he was born as to the externall and mortall body
items.note: The visible World is called man's 'parent' as to the outer, mortal body; man is a pattern of it.

items.quote: The soul is the off-spring and image of God.
items.note: Margin note on the soul as God's offspring and image.

items.name: Apoc. 22.
items.quote: Apoc. 22.
items.note: Margin reference beside God as Creator above man.

items.quote: Man who is a true Proteus of a fickle & wavering disposition received a flexible mind from Nature
items.note: Man is called a Proteus: of changeable disposition, able to rise or sink.

items.name: Eccl. 15.14.
items.note: Margin reference beside man's flexible mind; the same reference stands in the text later in MICRO.10.

items.quote: he might be regenerated into a quiet Angell or, the Forger of his fortune winding and creeping downward degenerate into a restlesse Bruite
items.note: Two outcomes: regenerated upward into an angel by grace, or degenerated into a brute.

items.name: Gen 2.
items.quote: Gen 2.
items.note: Margin reference beside man neglecting the fatherly admonition.

items.quote: turning from the mean to (the extreame) himselfe, dispising his Creator
items.note: The fall is described as turning from 'the mean' to oneself as an extreme.

items.quote: learned by experience what his own proper Evill and Nothing was to his voluntary damage and perdition, like a Thief and Robber
items.note: Man learns his own 'Evill and Nothing' by experience; likened to a thief and robber.

items.quote: theft and robbery of himselfe, and death
items.note: The margin note names the two 'inconveniences' of seeking what is another's: theft and robbery of oneself, and death; much of the note is gaps.

items.quote: like Lucifer, not content with his lot, ambitiously desiring higher things, he set himselfe in opposition against God
items.note: Man's fall compared to Lucifer's.

items.quote: cast out of the Garden of pleasures into this dolefull and darksome valley of Misery and Ignorance
items.note: The fall ends in expulsion into a valley of Misery and Ignorance.

items.name: Eccl.
items.quote: The first man was left in the hand of his own counsell (Eccl. 15.14.)
items.note: Scripture reference given in the text for man left to his own counsel.

items.name: Herms and Moses
items.quote: greedily desired the possession of good and evill to his own destruction, as Herms and Moses
items.note: Herms and Moses named as showing the first man's fall; the book spells 'Herms' here and 'Hermes' in MICRO.9.

items.quote: Man, the bond or buckle of the world, the last wonderfull and honourable living creature
items.what: the bond or buckle of the world
items.note: Man named the bond or buckle of the world, made last.

items.quote: God created man that the number and losse of the rebellious Angells might be made up
items.note: Margin note: man created to make up the number of the fallen angels.

items.quote: out of the slime of the Earth or visible frame of the whole consisting of Heaven or Heavenly Sphaeres and the Earth
items.note: The 'slime of the Earth' (è limo terrae) is glossed as the visible frame of the whole, heaven and earth together, not earth alone.

items.quote: viz. out of the most thin or pure substance of the whole frame of the world concentred into one body
items.note: What man was made of: the purest substance of the whole world drawn together into one body.

items.quote: fashioned by the great Spacyrus into a bodily shape, made to supply the place of the fallen Angells
items.note: The maker of man is named 'the great Spacyrus'.

items.quote: Man was formed of the most excellent Compound and purest Extract of the whole Word, out of the Center of all Circles
items.note: Man's making is told in terms of Compound and purest Extract; 'Word' stands where 'world' is used elsewhere in the sentence.

items.name: Nazianzen
items.quote: God made Man last, that in him, as in a short and briefe way, he might set out or expresse all that before he had made at large
items.note: Nazianzen: man made last as a brief summary of all creation.

items.quote: the Microcosm or Limus Terrae, Man is compacted of all bodies and created things
items.note: Microcosm and Limus Terrae are given as names for man, who is compacted of all bodies, like an oration of letters.

items.quote: took the Quintessence out of all things created and thereof fashioned and composed Man as the Prince and End of all these
items.note: God took the Quintessence of all created things and made man from it.

items.quote: In respect of the Body or corruptible Nature he bears the Image of the great, sensible and temporall World
items.note: Man's body images the great world.

items.quote: the Archetype or originall copy and patterne of the world, that is, of the immortall Wisdome of God himselfe
items.note: Archetype is defined as the original pattern of the world, the immortal Wisdom of God; man's soul bears its image.

items.quote: all the properties of Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls entred into him
items.note: Man holds the properties of the three kinds of things.

items.quote: God is all things of himselfe; Man is made all things of God
items.note: A contrast: God is all things of himself, man all things by God.

items.quote: Man is the tye, bond, knot, joynt
items.what: the tye, bond, knot, joynt, packet or bundle of all the Creatures
items.note: Man named the tie or bundle of all creatures.

items.name: Psal. 8.
items.quote: Psal. 8. Thou hast put all things under his
items.note: Margin reference beside man as the bond of all creatures.

items.name: Parace[gap]s.
items.quote: excepteth the Spirits and inhabitant of the
items.note: A margin note names Parace(gap)s. as making an exception (the spirits and inhabitants of the elements, partly a gap) to all things being put under man.

items.quote: they respect and honour him as Gods steward set over the Orchard or Garden of this world
items.note: Man is God's steward over the world's garden.

items.quote: all the works of the Divine goodnesse are circular and perfect, sphaerically wheeled about to him from whom they proceeded
items.note: God's works are circular, returning to their source.

items.quote: He is the Centre in that all things flow from him, and because the Essence of all things pierceth also through all things
items.note: Why God is called the Centre.

items.quote: He is the Circle, because like an all-capacious Tabernacle he concludeth and comprehendeth all things.
items.note: Why God is called the Circle.

items.quote: God the Centre and Circle of all things.
items.what: God the Centre and Circle of all things
items.note: Margin heading for the passage.

items.quote: Within God are all things, and at the worlds end nothing shall be without him
items.note: All things are within God; at the end nothing outside him.

items.quote: So is Man.
items.note: Margin note carrying the Centre and Circle over to man.

items.quote: Thus Man in imitation of his Creator is the Centre of the Creatures, and the Circle of them all.
items.note: Man, imitating God, is Centre and Circle of the creatures.

items.quote: It was Gods pleasure that all things which he made should honour him by Man.
items.note: Margin note: all things honour God through man.

items.quote: on him all the Sphaeres bestow their beams, operations, reflections and influences, and on him all the Creatures poure their vertues and effects
items.note: The spheres and creatures pour their influences and virtues upon man.

items.quote: as upon a middle Point and Retinacle or that by which they are stayed and supported
items.note: Retinacle is glossed as that by which things are stayed and supported.

items.quote: As the Earth is a Receptive body of all seeds, so also is Man.
items.note: Margin note likening man to the earth as receiver of all seeds.

items.quote: Man is said to be the Circle in that he containeth all things in himselfe
items.note: Why man is called the Circle.

items.quote: leadeth back all things that gushed out of that Summum Bonum, or chiefest good, unto the fountaine of Eternity
items.note: Summum Bonum glossed as chiefest good; man leads all things back to their source.
